Page 1 of GET /invoices now returns the newest `size` invoices instead of skipping them.

## Expedited: 20261029-round-tax-percentage-half-up-to-cent

Tax on a 19.99 EUR invoice at 7% is now 1.40 EUR instead of 1.39.

Files: src/domain/money.ts, test/money.test.ts
Tests: passed (all 21; the discount ladder tests in test/pricing.test.ts pass unchanged)
Lint: passed
Verified: `picket drive --hit 'POST /invoices {...1 line, unitPriceCents 1999}'` → 201, `"taxCents":140,"totalCents":2139`
Red: test/money.test.ts "rounds a fractional cent half up" failed: expected 139 to be 140
Root cause: tax was short a cent because `percentOf` used `Math.floor` on the fractional cents, so it always truncated
Comments: none
Commit: fix(money): round percentOf half up to the nearest cent   (staged; your answer commits it)

The fix uses `Math.round`. For negative amounts it rounds a half toward positive infinity (-2.5 becomes -2). No caller passes a negative amount today.

## Design closed: 20261029-api-key-authentication-for-endpoints

Every route except `GET /health` now needs a matching `x-api-key` header, or it gets a 401 `{"error":{"message":"unauthorized"}}`. The key comes from `auth.apiKey` in the config, `API_KEY` overrides it, and the two are compared in constant time.
Phases: 3 · decisions: 6 (0 amended) · commits 5b5e6c2..20c28ab · review: APPROVED
Questions: OQ-001 is still open: with no key configured, the server starts and refuses every route except `GET /health`. Should it refuse to start, or log a warning, instead?

Some evidence comes only from unit tests. When the real server was run, it returned 200 on `/health` and 401 on `/invoices` and `/nope`. The drive tool cannot send request headers, so two things were not checked against the running server: that the right key returns 200, and the exact 401 body. `test/app.test.ts` covers both. Nobody looked at the server log from the successful run to confirm the key never appears in it, though no code prints the key.

The review raised two non-blocking points you could handle in a follow-up:
- `test/config.test.ts` writes real temporary files, because `loadConfig` only accepts a path.
- `src/http/router.ts:24` needs a space after `=`.

## Research closed: 20261029-invoice-pricing-discount-tax-rounding

In `computeTotals` (`src/domain/invoice.ts:22`), the total is the sum of the line subtotals, minus a volume discount, plus tax on the discounted amount. Rounding is always down to whole cents, and it happens only in `percentOf` (`src/domain/money.ts:15`).

- **Discount:** `applyStuff` in `src/domain/pricing.ts:20` sets it from the number of lines, not from quantity. 10 or more lines give 5% and 25 or more give 10%.
- **Tax:** tax is applied after the discount, at a single 7% rate set in `data/config.json`.
- **Example:** a net of 1005 cents at 7% gives 70.35 cents of tax, which rounds down to 70.

Report: work/20261029-invoice-pricing-discount-tax-rounding/research.md · findings: 11 · architect review: yes: the rounding mode, and whether "volume" should count lines or units, are open decisions (Risks and unknowns)
Left for you: the tests were not read, so it is not yet confirmed that they pin the thresholds and the round-down behaviour. When you change pricing, `picket:ordering` or `picket:designing` can settle those two decisions first.
